title: A lambda that adapts a legacy comparer to Comparator

blocks.text: The page's Q5 shows that when the target interface is a functional interface, a lambda can be the whole adapter. Here the legacy code answers only one question, `lessThan(a, b)`, while `Comparator<String>` needs a negative, zero or positive `int`.
Write `Comparers.asComparator(legacy)`, returning a `Comparator<String>` that translates each call into `lessThan` questions (a lambda is enough):

items: **zero when neither is less by the legacy rule**, which may call two different strings equal.

blocks.text: With a legacy comparer that orders by length:

cases.says: With a legacy comparer that orders by length, the comparator is negative for ("a", "bb") and finds "a" as the minimum.
When neither string is less by the legacy rule, compare returns 0, even for different strings of the same length.
When the second string is less, compare returns a positive number.

concepts: When the target is a functional interface, a lambda or method reference can be the whole adapter, translating parameters and results.
